scenario: AITA for not ending my friendship with my best friend after he cheated on my sister? | Both my best friend and my sister know about my other account so this is a throwaway. I'm an 18 year old guy and I have a twin sister. I've been best friends with my best friend (we'll call him G) since kindergarten, so G and my sister have always been pretty close too. They've kind of had a "thing" going on our whole lives. For the longest time, they never officially dated for a bunch of different reasons I won't get into, but they were always really close and really into each other. A little over a year ago, when we were all 17, they finally started dating. Everything went really well for like 13 months, but then long story short, G cheated on my sister and I was the one who figured it out. He swore it wouldn't happen again and begged me not to tell my sister but I told her anyway. I was mad at him and he was mad at me so we didn't talk for a month and a half, which was honestly the weirdest month and a half of my whole life. G's practically like my brother, we've been inseparable since kindergarten, so not having him around was kinda....unbearable honestly lol After our streak of not talking to each other, G invited me on his family ski trip as a way to make amends (I've been on lots of his family's ski trips through the years). I accepted and ended up forgiving him and letting him back into my life because it was way too weird without him in it. I can tell he's genuinely sorry about what happened. He literally cried cause he felt so bad and I've only seen him cry like once before in my whole life Anyway, G and my sister broke up as soon as she found out he cheated and they're still not on speaking terms, so my sister obviously isn't happy about the whole situation. She's making me feel like shit for still being friends with G, and she doesn't seem to understand how big of a deal it would be for us to lose our 13 year friendship over her. I know G made a huge mistake, I hate him for it and I'll never 100% get over it, but I'm not gonna let it ruin my best and longest friendship. I think about it like this: if your best friend cheated on their SO and then felt like shit, would you end your friendship with them? No. So why is this any different just because his SO happened to be my sister? G and I are going to the same college in the fall (a different college in a different state than the one my sister's going to), so none of this is gonna be something that we even think about when we're living in different places Am I the asshole?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being an asshole in this situation. Let me start by laying out the facts as I understand them. I'm an 18-year-old guy with a twin sister. My best friend, G, and my sister have had a close relationship since kindergarten. They never officially dated for a long time but were always really into each other. About a year ago, when we were all 17, they finally started dating. Everything was great for about 13 months, but then G cheated on my sister. I was the one who found out about it. G begged me not to tell my sister, but I did. I was mad at him, and he was mad at me, so we didn't talk for a month and a half. That was the weirdest time of my life because G is practically like my brother, and not having him around was really hard. After that, G invited me on his family's ski trip as a way to make amends. I went, and after that, I forgave him and let him back into my life because it was too weird without him. I can tell he's genuinely sorry about what happened. He even cried because he felt so bad, and I've only seen him cry once before in my whole life. Now, G and my sister broke up as soon as she found out he cheated, and they're still not speaking. My sister is making me feel like shit for still being friends with G. She doesn't seem to understand how big of a deal it would be for us to lose our 13-year friendship over her. I know G made a huge mistake, and I hate him for it. I'll never 100% get over it, but I'm not going to let it ruin my best and longest friendship. I think about it like this: if your best friend cheated on their SO and felt like shit, would you end your friendship with them? No. So why is this any different just because his SO happened to be my sister? G and I are going to the same college in the fall, a different college in a different state than the one my sister's going to. So none of this is going to be something we even think about when we're living in different places. Am I the asshole here? I need to figure out if I'm being unreasonable or if my sister is overreacting. Let me break it down. First, G cheated on my sister. That's a serious betrayal. My sister is hurt, and she's angry. She's making me feel bad for still being friends with G. But I've known G since kindergarten, and he's practically my brother. We've been through a lot together, and losing that friendship would be devastating for me. I forgave G because I saw how genuinely sorry he was. He cried, which is rare for him. I think he's learned from his mistake, and I don't want to lose him over something that happened between him and my sister. I also don't want to be the one who ends a 13-year friendship because of someone else's actions. On the other hand, my sister feels betrayed, and she's probably still hurt. She might feel like I'm not standing up for her by continuing the friendship. She might think that by staying friends with G, I'm minimizing the betrayal or not taking her feelings seriously. I wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I can maintain the friendship but also support my sister. But she's not talking to G, so it's hard to see how that would work. I also don't want to choose sides between my sister and my best friend. That's a tough spot to be in. I think about how friendships work. If my best friend did something wrong, but they apologized and showed genuine remorse, would I end the friendship? Probably not. I would try to move past it, especially if the friendship is as long-standing as mine with G. So why should it be different just because the person they wronged is my sister? Also, considering we're going to different colleges, the situation might naturally fade into the background. We'll be in different places, and the issue might not come up as much. That makes me think that holding onto the friendship is a good idea for both of us. But I also have to consider my sister's feelings. She's my twin, and our relationship is important. I don't want to damage that either. Maybe I need to talk to her about why I'm choosing to keep the friendship and see if we can find a way to both be okay with it. In the end, I think I'm not the asshole. I'm prioritizing a long-term friendship that's meant a lot to me, and I'm trying to move past a mistake that G has already shown he's sorry for. My sister's feelings are valid, but I also have the right to maintain my own relationships, especially one that's been so significant.
